headline: Bank defaulted loans exceed 6 lakh crore taka again
summary: Nearly 33% of total bank loans in Bangladesh have become defaulted, putting depositors' money at risk as irregularities surface.
details: Defaulted loans in the banking sector have once again crossed 6 lakh crore taka. According to Bangladesh Bank, these loans increased by 17,851 crore taka between March and June of this year.

Currently, 32.78% of all bank loans are defaulted, meaning nearly 33 taka out of every 100 taka lent is now unrecoverable. This massive amount of capital is no longer contributing to the economy, leaving depositors' funds in jeopardy.

Experts suggest that the political change in August 2024 has exposed long-standing irregularities, fraud, and anonymous loans. Many problematic loans were previously hidden through rescheduling and accounting adjustments.
Five merged banks—Exim, Social Islami, First Security Islami, Global Islami, and Union Bank—are in the worst condition, with over 80% of their total loans being defaulted.
Several other banks, including Basic, Janata, AB Bank, and Islami Bank, also report default rates exceeding 50%. Many of these issues are linked to influential business groups and political figures.
The top 20 defaulting institutions include 11 entities controlled by the S Alam Group, along with companies owned by Salman F. Rahman and other high-profile individuals.
The scale of the crisis has grown dramatically over time. Defaulted loans were only 22,481 crore taka in 2009, skyrocketing to over 6 lakh crore taka by June 2024.

Five merged banks—Exim, Social Islami, First Security Islami, Global Islami, and Union Bank—are in the worst condition, with over 80% of their total loans being defaulted.

Several other banks, including Basic, Janata, AB Bank, and Islami Bank, also report default rates exceeding 50%. Many of these issues are linked to influential business groups and political figures.

The top 20 defaulting institutions include 11 entities controlled by the S Alam Group, along with companies owned by Salman F. Rahman and other high-profile individuals.

headline: Asif Mahmud threatens defamation suit against ACC over corruption claims
summary: The former advisor and NCP spokesperson demands the withdrawal of news reports based on ACC statements within 24 hours, calling the allegations 'politically motivated'.
details: Former advisor and National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has demanded that news reports based on statements from the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) be withdrawn within 24 hours.
Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Mahmud called the reports 'formulaic' and claimed they lacked specific information and did not align with the ACC's own allegations.
He denied allegations of corruption regarding promotions and transfers, stating that all such processes were conducted according to government rules and through the Public Service Commission (PSC).
Mahmud alleged that he is being framed for political reasons, claiming the reports have caused him social and political defamation.

He pointed out that an ACC deputy director had initially mentioned the truth of the allegations to a media outlet but later requested via WhatsApp not to publish the information, which Mahmud says proves a lack of evidence.
The NCP spokesperson warned of legal action against those involved if the news reports are not withdrawn by the media and if the ACC does not take steps to retract them.

He compared the current situation to the 'old tactics' of the Awami League government, claiming he is being harassed politically in the same way the previous government targeted Khaleda Zia with corruption cases.
caption:
Asif Mahmud gives a 24-hour ultimatum to the ACC and media outlets to retract corruption allegations or face a defamation lawsuit.

Former advisor and National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has demanded that news reports based on statements from the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) be withdrawn within 24 hours.

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Mahmud called the reports 'formulaic' and claimed they lacked specific information and did not align with the ACC's own allegations.

He denied allegations of corruption regarding promotions and transfers, stating that all such processes were conducted according to government rules and through the Public Service Commission (PSC).

Mahmud alleged that he is being framed for political reasons, claiming the reports have caused him social and political defamation.

He pointed out that an ACC deputy director had initially mentioned the truth of the allegations to a media outlet but later requested via WhatsApp not to publish the information, which Mahmud says proves a lack of evidence.

The NCP spokesperson warned of legal action against those involved if the news reports are not withdrawn by the media and if the ACC does not take steps to retract them.

He compared the current situation to the 'old tactics' of the Awami League government, claiming he is being harassed politically in the same way the previous government targeted Khaleda Zia with corruption cases.
